title: General.
officialText:
A masonry chimney is a chimney constructed of concrete or masonry, hereinafter referred to as “masonry.”
Masonry chimneys shall be constructed, anchored, supported and reinforced as required in this chapter.
Chimneys shall be designed and constructed so as to provide the necessary draft and capacity for each appliance connected to
them to completely exhaust the products of combustion to the outside air. The temperature on adjacent combustible surfaces shall
not be raised above 160°F (71°C). Chimney and vents shall be designed to resist the effects of condensation that would cause
deterioration of the chimney or vent.
In any case, the outlet shall be arranged so that the flue gases are not directed so that they jeopardize people, overheat co m-
bustible structures, or enter building openings in the vicinity of the outlet. Gas-fired appliances shall be vented in accordance with
this code, the New York City Fuel Gas Code and NFPA 54.
Chimneys shall not be supported by the equipment they serve unless such equipment has been specifically designed for such
loads.
